cleanIntro: TriStar's own field disassembly for its 12- and 20-gauge gas autoloader, then the cleaning it calls for section by section. Every step below carries the manual's words and the page they sit on.

steps.title: Safety on, then prove it empty in three places
steps.action: Push the safety button fully to the right so it protrudes from the right side of the trigger guard, then check the chamber, the elevator and the magazine tube — by eye and by finger — before you touch anything else.
steps.prose: Three places, not one. A gas gun holds shells in the tube long after the chamber is clear, and the elevator can be carrying one you never see.
steps.quote: Position the safety button so it is protruding fully out the right side of the trigger guard indicating the "ON" (SAFE) position, and visually and physically check the chamber, elevator and magazine tube to be certain the shotgun is unloaded before disassembling the firearm.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — DISASSEMBLY, PDF p.12 — the manual prints no page numbers
steps.warn: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning.

steps.title: Empty the magazine tube through the shell stop
steps.action: Turn the shotgun so the trigger guard faces up, push the elevator down and hold it there, then depress the front of the shell stop on the side of the receiver opposite the ejection port to release one shell at a time.
steps.prose: The shells come out under spring pressure, one per press, so keep your hand where the shell will land rather than chasing it off the bench.
steps.caution: Repeat until the tube is empty, then re-check the chamber and elevator.
steps.quote: While holding the elevator down, depress the front of the shell stop located on the opposite side of the receiver from the ejection port. This will release one shell from the magazine tube under spring pressure.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — TO UNLOAD, PDF p.11 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Lock the bolt back
steps.action: Pull the bolt operating handle back as far as it goes; it should stay locked to the rear on its own.
steps.prose: If it does not stay back, stop — the action is not holding, and that is a fault to sort out before the gun comes apart.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt operating handle back as far as it will go; it should stay locked.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE FOREARM, PDF p.12 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Magazine cap off, forearm forward
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap counter-clockwise, take it off the end of the magazine tube, then slide the forearm toward the muzzle and off.
steps.prose: Counter-clockwise from behind the gun. The cap is only finger-tight when correctly fitted, so it should not need a tool.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap (counter clockwise) and remove it.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE FOREARM, PDF p.12 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Barrel out, gas piston with it
steps.action: Hold the operating handle, press the bolt release button, let the bolt travel slowly fully forward, and with the bolt forward pull the barrel out of the receiver with the gas piston still assembled in the gas cylinder portion of the barrel.
steps.prose: Riding the bolt down rather than letting it slam is the whole point of holding the handle. If the piston stays behind on the magazine tube, slide it forward off the tube.
steps.caution: If the gas piston remains on the magazine tube after the barrel is removed slide the gas piston forward to remove it.
steps.quote: With the bolt fully forward, pull the barrel out of the receiver with the gas piston assembled in the gas cylinder portion of the barrel
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE BARREL, PDF p.12 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Line up the notch and pull the operating handle
steps.action: Push the action back slowly until the notch in the bolt lines up with the raised protrusion on the operating handle, then pull the operating handle straight out.
steps.prose: Straight out, not levered. The handle only clears when the notch and the protrusion agree, so if it resists, the bolt is in the wrong place rather than stuck.
steps.quote: Slowly push the action (bolt action slide and bolt assembly) back until the notch in the bolt lines up with the raised protrusion on the operating handle
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE BOLT, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Bolt and slide out through the barrel hole
steps.action: Let the bolt action slide and bolt assembly travel slowly fully forward, draw them out of the receiver through the barrel hole, then lift the bolt assembly off the bolt action slide.
steps.prose: They come out the front, not the bottom. The two separate by lifting once they are clear of the receiver.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt action slide and bolt assembly from the receiver through the barrel hole. Lift the bolt assembly from the bolt action slide.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE BOLT, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Push the trigger housing pin out
steps.action: Push the trigger housing retaining pin out with a blunt object no larger than 1/8 inch; it will go from either direction.
steps.prose: Blunt is the operative word — a sharp punch marks the receiver and does not move the pin any better.
steps.quote: The pin can be pushed out from either directon.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, step 1, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Trigger housing forward and down
steps.action: Push the bolt release button and slide the trigger housing assembly forward and down out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The bolt release has to be held in or the housing will not clear. Forward first, then down — trying to drop it straight out binds it.
steps.caution: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by pushing the bolt release button and sliding the trigger housing assembly forward and down.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, step 2, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers

steps.title: Do not take the trigger housing apart
steps.action: Stop at the housing as an assembly. TriStar states it is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled, and that any disassembly of it belongs to an authorized Product Service Center or a qualified gunsmith.
steps.prose: This is a prohibition, not a difficulty rating. Brushing the outside of the housing is the cleaning the manual asks for.
steps.quote: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers
steps.warn: Never pull the trigger while the trigger housing is removed from the receiver.

steps.title: Field disassembly complete
steps.action: Barrel with gas piston, forearm, magazine cap, bolt assembly, bolt action slide, operating handle and trigger housing — that is the whole disassembly TriStar publishes for routine cleaning.
steps.prose: The manual draws the line here itself, and it draws it for maintenance, not just for warranty.
steps.quote: Field disassembly is now complete. The shotgun should not be disassembled any further for routine cleaning or maintenance.
steps.cite: TriStar Semi-Automatic Shotgun Instruction Manual — 12-20 Gauge Autoloading Shotgun — ABSENT — no revision or part code printed anywhere in the document — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers

deepAbsentReason: TriStar's manual ends its disassembly at "Field disassembly is now complete. The shotgun should not be disassembled any further for routine cleaning or maintenance" (PDF p.13 — the manual prints no page numbers), and states that further disassembly should only be performed at an authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith. It separately forbids taking the trigger housing assembly apart at all. So this listing has NO deep clean: the manual documents no procedure past the field strip, and inventing one is not an option.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND GAS CYLINDER
tasks: Remove the gas piston from the gas cylinder portion of the barrel
Scrub the bore, chamber and gas cylinder bore with solvent, then follow with cleaning patches until barrel and gas cylinder bore are clean
Place a few drops of light oil in the gas cylinder bore
Finish with a lightly oiled patch through the bore and chamber for a protective coating — a stiff brass bristle brush handles stubborn deposits
Leave no patches or excess oil or grease in the bore: TriStar warns these create dangerous obstructions

cleaning.name: ACTION AND RECEIVER
tasks: Clean all components of the action including the bolt assembly and bolt action slide to remove accumulated residue, using an evaporating solvent
Use lubrication sparingly on action parts — they stay cleaner longer
Clean the inside of the receiver with a rag or soft brush, paying special attention to the tracks which guide the bolt and slide, then place a few drops of light oil in those tracks
Never use a brush with metal bristles on the receiver or trigger housing — it removes the protective coating

cleaning.name: TRIGGER HOUSING (OUTSIDE ONLY)
tasks: Brush loose residue from the trigger housing with a soft bristle brush
Never pull the trigger while the trigger housing is removed from the receiver
Do not disassemble the trigger housing assembly

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM
tasks: Thoroughly clean the magazine tube, gas piston, piston ring, seal and gas action return spring using solvent; a stiff brass bristle brush shifts stubborn deposits
Apply a light coat of gun oil to all metal parts, then wipe thoroughly with a dry cloth
Keep it dry: excess oil accelerates carbon build-up in the gas system and can hurt performance

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE
tasks: Keep the precision threads on the choke tube clean and lightly oiled at all times
Have a choke tube properly installed while cleaning the barrel, to avoid residue building up on the threads
Check choke tube tightness periodically

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: TriStar recommends a thorough cleaning after every 200 rounds
Clean more often in dusty, dirty or harsh conditions, or with ammunition that leaves heavy powder residue
Clean and oil thoroughly before long storage, and do not plug the barrel or store in a fabric-lined case

reassembly: Assemble the bolt assembly onto the bolt action slide, then the bolt action slide onto the magazine tube.

Push the bolt action slide slowly into the receiver, look through the ejection port and align the notch in the slide with the notch in the bolt, then align the operating handle's raised protrusion with the notch in the bolt and push the handle in.

Insert the trigger housing assembly by pressing the bolt release button while pushing the housing up and rearward, then push the trigger housing pin in until it is flush with the sides of the receiver.

Mount the barrel: check the gas piston is correctly assembled and oriented in the gas cylinder portion of the barrel, slide the barrel into the receiver with the gas cylinder on the magazine tube, and pull the operating handle half way back to seat it fully.
Pull the operating handle back so the action stays open, slide the forearm over the magazine tube and seat it into the receiver, then screw the magazine cap on finger-tight.
fncheck: TriStar states it plainly on PDF p.3: after any work on the firearm — cleaning, adjustments, disassembly, or fitting an accessory — the shotgun should be re-checked for proper functioning before firing live ammunition.
